raw_response:
I am 50 years old. I never went to school. I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years, since I married into this village. My husband and I do the work, and we hire the machine for planting and harvest. My daughter-in-law works in a factory in Handan and sends money home. My son helps when he is not working construction in the city.

I learned everything by watching my mother-in-law and the neighbors. I do not trust books or outsiders. I trust my eyes. If Old Wang's wheat looks better than mine, I ask him what he put on it. That is how I decide.

Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu. My corn gave me about 600 kg per mu. This year I will do almost the same, but I will water the corn one extra time because last August was too dry and the corn shriveled on the top.

For my 8 mu of winter wheat, I will use the improved seed from the village supply shop. I cannot read the bag, but I know it is the one with the yellow picture that costs 3.5 yuan per jin. I sow about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I hire the rotary tiller for 50 yuan per mu to turn the ground. Then I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. The bag is 100 jin. I do not know what numbers are on it, but the dealer calls it the "three 15s." Then at Qingming, when the wheat starts shooting up, I spread half a bag of urea on each mu. Half a bag is 50 jin. I used to put only 30 jin, but Old Wang put 50 jin three years ago and his wheat heads were bigger than mine, so now I do 50 jin. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than lose grain. Fertilizer costs money, but a bad harvest is a disaster for my family.

I will water the wheat three times. Once after planting if the autumn is dry. Once in spring when it is jointing. Once when the heads are filling and the grain is swelling. Everyone in the village does three times. The well pump uses electricity, but three times is necessary.

I spray pesticide twice on the wheat. Once for weeds when the wheat is small. Once for aphids or rust when I see them on the leaves. Last year I only sprayed once and the aphids came thick in July.

For my 8 mu of summer corn, I plant hybrid seed. I buy the seed in small bags. Each mu takes about 3 jin of seed. Right after the wheat harvest in June, the machine drills the corn into the wheat stubble. I do not till for corn. The rotary tiller costs money and time, and the stubble helps keep the moisture in the ground. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. Then when the corn is knee-high — around late July — I spread 50 jin of urea per mu. Last year I only used 40 jin urea and the ears were small at the tip. This year I will use 50 jin.

I will irrigate the corn twice. Once after planting if it does not rain within three days. Once when it is tasseling in late July or early August. Last year I only watered once and the dry August burned the leaves.

I spray corn twice. Once for weeds when it is small. Once for armyworm in August. The armyworm comes every year if you do not spray.

I expect my wheat to yield 550 kg per mu and my corn to yield 650 kg per mu. Last year corn was 600 kg, but the extra water and urea should help. I hope the grain price is good. If fertilizer gets more expensive next year, I might have to cut back. But this year I will do it this way.
